newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 5.

text.p: Lawyers try to sell Morgan interviews: Lawyers acting for NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan were on Wednesday night revealed as trying to sell exclusive interviews with him for at least NZ$20,000, according to conversations recorded by TV3. Page 1.
Warring MPs displease Clark: Labour leader Helen Clark moved on Wednesday to stop senior MP Mike Moore and newcomer Tariana Turia warring publicly over Maori issues. Page 2.
Super survey results buoy Peters: Treasurer Winston Peters was "enormously encouraged" by survey results showing about 30 percent support for a compulsory scheme, he said on Wednesday. Page 2.
Inquiry cost 'will bring returns': Treasurer Winston Peters said on Wednesday that for every "dollar down", the taxpayer would get $25 back from the Cook Islands tax commission of inquiry. Page 17.
Fletcher Energy mum on retail petrol market entry rumours: Fletcher Energy remained tight-lipped on Wednesday over reports the company was gearing up to enter the retail petrol market. Page 17.

State servants told: shred papers: Cabinet ministers are reported to have instructed public servants to destroy documents because of fears details would be revealed under the Official Information Act.
Costly first two years for Ergo: The discount mortgage lender, Ergo Personal Financial Services has made a $15 million loss in its first two years of operation.

Savings boost coming soon: Future growth in retirement savings will be much stronger regardless of the outcome of the vote on compulsory superannuation in September, the general manager of ANZ Funds Management, Anthony Quirk, said.
Asian Properties set to swim in $94m cash pool: Asian Properties should be floating in $94 million of cash at the end of next week, but was still selling at a discount to that asset on Wednesday.

F&P expects profit fall: Equity analysts expect the use of the New Zealand dollar against its Australian counterpart in the past year to hold whiteware manufacturer Fisher and Paykel to a slightly lower March-year profit than expected.
MP 'relaxed' over criticism: Labour MP Mike Moore defended himself on Wednesday against an attack from within his own party over an "evil" stance on Maori rights issues. Page 2.

Call to shift funds into child health: A series of one-day summits nationwide will help the government develop a national child-health strategy, Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton said on Wednesday. Page 6.
